chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: When a man drinks wine, he becomes intoxicated; and when he is intoxicated, he raves; and when he raves, he fabricates (lies); so flog him with the penalty of the fabricator.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal reasoning for the penalty of drinking wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and transmitted via the reliable chain of Zurara, this hadith establishes the legal rationale for the hadd of khamr by linking intoxication to the loss of cognitive control and subsequent fabrication of falsehoods. This causal progression justifies punishing the drinker with the penalty of the 'fabricator' (al-muftari), reflecting the Shia juristic view that the sin lies in the degradation of the self and truthfulness caused by wine. The narration underscores the spiritual and legal gravity of wine as a gateway to major sins, a concept deeply rooted in the Imams' teachings on character corruption.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Aliasws was saying that the man, when he drinks the wine, gets intoxicated, and when he is intoxicated, raves, and when he raves, he fabricates, therefore he would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd) of the fabricator’.
